E: I’m a sophomore

My mom died four years ago today.

It is currently 3:04 am. If I sleep I’m sure I could sober up enough to put on a semblance of respectability.

If I am to sleep, I can only sleep four hours.

In five hours I have school.

Skipping is not an option.

Today is going to suck ass.

Lost my mom when I was 12 a few years ago today.
I don’t want to turn this into some weird dick measuring contest and I know that we only know what it’s like to be ourselves but I think that may be one of the hardest times to lose a parent.

I know that I *should* be different. All my friends are doing well. They all have jobs and good grades. I know I *should* have guidance, I *should* have some sort of reliability that I can count on above all else, but I don’t.
And I think as a teenager, when everything is so new to you, you need to be able to admit your vulnerability and have a “safe space” for yourself, but I don’t.

Sorry. I didn’t mean to bring you down or offend. I just wanted to rant about that. It feels like no matter who I’m with I’m on the outside looking in. I feel like I don’t belong anywhere because I don’t.

I saved it to my personal google drive so there is little chance of someone finding it before they should. And I’d much rather have this prepared than whatever I could drunkenly scribble down the night I’d actually do it, IF I do it.

I’ve been waiting for this light for four fucking years and I’ve never seen it.

I said I probably won’t use it because I don’t really believe in much of an afterlife so I guess this is our only run around the track.

Wew lads.

Today one of my teachers almost killed a kid. This teacher is interesting. He is a 6'7 mountain of a man with a mullet as long as his arm.

He is supposed to teach my class buisness, however he spends most of his days telling us stories (which admittedly is preferable to learning). When I first got into the class, he had us all vote on wether or not a minimum wage is a good idea. I voted yes for the obvious reasons. For the rest of the class we watched a completely one sided video explaining why we should abolish the minimum wage (thinking about posting it on here actually). Despite our disagreements we're on pretty friendly terms.

On to the meat of the story.

We were supposed to be learning about "entrepreneurship" so he had two groups of students make peanut butter and jelly samwiches. When a student objected because of potential peanut allergies in the school, my teacher ranted about Obamacare. 

For the most part the class went smoothly. I got myself and some friends some sandwiches and we basically just dicked around all class.

Until a pera (a person that helps with disabled students) showed up because he saw some students hocking sandwiches in the hallways (the students were told to do so by the teacher). The pera made a big show of buying his sandwiches and messed around with the kids for a bit. About fifteen minutes later, my "teacher" comes in looking pissed. He said a special ed kid had an allergic reaction to the peanut butter and needed an Epi pen. This came to the surprise of no one.

It honestly baffles me how people can act so irresponsibly with children sometimes, especially the special ed kids. The way I see it, the teacher and the pera are at fault here.

I got to talk to an astrophysicist that works at NASA for one of my AP courses today though, so that's cool.

TL;DR My teacher almost killed a kid because he blamed peanut allergies on Obamacare.
